topic: Agentic plan-to-code preflight and adversarial certification: executable acceptance criteria, simulation, negative-space review, evidence gates, human override, and regression traceability
research_questions: How do mature agentic engineering and safety systems turn plans into executable preflight checks, scenario simulations, and adversarial certification?
Which acceptance-criteria, negative-space, evidence-gate, human-override, and regression-traceability patterns are documented by primary sources?
How should a plan-to-code gate expose blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified outcomes without conflating them?
What evidence is necessary to claim that a plan remains safe and complete as implementation and dependencies change?

sources.title: AI RMF Core
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.material_relevance: Defines govern, map, measure, and manage across the AI lifecycle, including go or no-go decisions, human oversight, testing, uncertainty, independent review, monitoring, override, and change management.

sources.title: Our updated Preparedness Framework
sources.material_relevance: Documents thresholded capability evaluation, safeguards reports, automated and expert-led evaluations, safety review recommendations, deployment decisions, and reassessment when new evidence appears.

sources.title: Introducing the Frontier Safety Framework
sources.material_relevance: Documents critical capability levels, periodic early-warning evaluations, threshold-triggered mitigation plans, deployment-context balancing, and iterative framework updates.

sources.title: Agentic AI – Threats and Mitigations
sources.material_relevance: Provides a threat-model-based reference for emerging agentic threats and mitigations, supporting adversarial and negative-space review of tool-using systems.

sources.title: About protected branches
sources.material_relevance: Documents enforceable merge gates for reviews, status checks, conversation resolution, signatures, deployments, stale approval invalidation, latest-push approval, and merge queues.

sources.title: About GitHub Copilot code review
sources.material_relevance: Documents that agent review can miss problems, requires careful validation and human review, and can be configured to re-review new commits.

sources.title: Get started with Copilot agents on GitHub
sources.material_relevance: Shows an issue-to-pull-request agent workflow with visible session changes, human review, iterative correction, and explicit approval before merge.

sources.title: Reviewing dependency changes in a pull request
sources.material_relevance: Documents dependency diffs, vulnerability impact, and an enforceable action that fails a pull request when newly introduced dependencies have known vulnerabilities.

sources.title: Provenance
sources.material_relevance: Defines verifiable provenance that traces built artifacts to source and describes source provenance for change-management history.

sources.title: Build: Verifying artifacts
sources.material_relevance: Documents verification of trusted builders, signatures, subjects, build types, external parameters, expectations, recursive dependencies, and continuous monitoring.

sources.title: Agent-SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of LLM Agents
sources.material_relevance: Provides a primary benchmark with 349 interaction environments, 2,000 test cases, eight safety-risk categories, ten failure modes, and agent safety results.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.material_relevance: Provides an executable software-engineering evaluation model grounded in real issues, pull requests, codebase edits, multi-file coordination, and execution environments.

findings.claim: NIST's AI RMF turns broad risk intent into a lifecycle loop: govern establishes accountability and policy, map establishes context and risks, measure uses documented tests and metrics, and manage allocates responses and continuous improvement. Map supports an initial go or no-go decision; measure calls for pre-deployment and recurring testing, uncertainty and benchmark reporting, independent review, production monitoring, safe failure, appeal, override, deactivation, recovery, and change management.
findings.notes: This is the clearest primary framework found for converting plan intent into preflight inputs, evidence requirements, lifecycle states, and re-evaluation triggers.

findings.claim: Thresholded safety systems use preflight evaluation before a decision boundary and attach mitigations to the result. Google DeepMind describes critical capability levels, periodic early-warning evaluations, and a mitigation plan when a threshold is crossed. OpenAI describes capability thresholds, safeguards reports, scalable automated evaluations plus expert deep dives, safety review recommendations, leadership decisions, and reassessment when new evidence changes the risk picture.
findings.notes: The shared pattern is a decision gate backed by named evaluations and mitigation evidence, rather than a single undifferentiated pass score.

findings.claim: A mature coding-agent workflow makes the plan-to-code transition observable and reviewable: GitHub's documented agent flow starts from an issue, produces a pull request, exposes session reasoning and file changes, requests review, supports iteration, and leaves approval and merge to a human. GitHub separately warns that AI code review is not guaranteed to find all problems and must be supplemented by human review; repeated review can be tied to each new commit.
findings.notes: This directly answers the human-override question: agent feedback is advisory, while human review and approval are separate control points.

findings.claim: GitHub protected branches demonstrate enforceable acceptance criteria at the merge boundary: required reviews, status checks, conversation resolution, signed commits, deployments, and code-owner approval can block a merge; stale approvals can be dismissed when the diff or merge base changes; a latest reviewable push can require a different approver; and a merge queue can re-run checks against the current target branch.
findings.notes: These controls provide concrete semantics for blocked and invalidated outcomes instead of treating an old pass as portable.

findings.claim: SLSA supplies a provenance and verification pattern for regression traceability: provenance records how an artifact was produced and traces it to source; verification checks trusted builder identity, signatures, artifact subject, predicate type, expected source and build parameters, and optionally dependencies recursively. SLSA also describes expectation comparison and continuous monitors for detecting changes.
findings.notes: The direct design consequence is that certification evidence must bind to immutable inputs and verifiable build or change provenance.

findings.claim: Agent-SafetyBench operationalizes adversarial scenario certification as a matrix rather than a prompt check: it reports 349 interaction environments and 2,000 test cases across eight safety-risk categories and ten common failure modes, and its evaluation of 16 agents found no safety score above 60%; the authors conclude that defense prompts alone can be insufficient.
findings.notes: The benchmark supports negative-space coverage through varied environments, interaction traces, failure-mode labels, and explicit safety scoring.

findings.claim: SWE-bench models executable plan-to-code acceptance as issue resolution in a real repository: the agent edits a codebase from an issue description, coordinates changes across functions, classes, and files, and interacts with an execution environment. Its reported results show that only the simplest issues were solved well, so textual plan agreement is not evidence of implementation completeness.
findings.notes: This is evidence for execution-grounded acceptance harnesses and held-out regression tasks, not evidence that any one benchmark is sufficient for certification.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Thresholded preflight with early-warning evaluations and attached mitigation plans.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A gate should expose the measured threshold, evaluation run, residual risk, and mitigation or disposition required by that threshold.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Issue-to-pull-request workflow with observable agent activity, human review, iterative correction, and explicit approval.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Plan completion should produce a reviewable change set and evidence trail; the agent's own report is not the approval.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Policy-enforced merge gates that invalidate or rerun approval when the proposed change, merge base, dependencies, or deployment state changes.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: The plan-to-code gate needs explicit invalidation and revalidation transitions, not just a permanent certified flag.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Artifact provenance plus expectation checking and recursive dependency verification.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Evidence gates can bind a plan, source revision, builder, dependency closure, and output digest so later consumers can independently verify what was certified.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Scenario matrices that exercise interaction environments and named failure modes, rather than a single happy-path test.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Adversarial certification should include tool misuse, permission boundaries, malformed inputs, unsafe side effects, and recovery behavior.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Treating an agent-generated review or self-reported success as proof of correctness or completeness.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Require independent human review for risk classes that demand it, executable acceptance checks, adversarial scenarios, and explicit evidence references before certification.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Reusing an approval after the reviewed diff, merge base, dependency set, or deployment context changed.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Hash plan and implementation inputs, detect change impact, revoke stale approval, and rerun affected checks against the current state.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Relying on prompts or a narrow happy-path simulation to control unsafe tool-using behavior.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Threat-model tools and side effects, then exercise negative-space scenarios and named failure modes in isolated environments with fail-safe handling.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Certifying an output without proving which source, builder, configuration, or dependencies produced it.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Require signed provenance, expected source and build parameters, dependency review, and recursive verification where the risk model requires it.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Collapsing unknown, unmeasured, or conflicting evidence into a binary pass state.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Represent unavailable metrics, uncertainty, residual risk, and conflicting evidence explicitly; default to blocked or uncertain until an authorized human disposition exists.

implications.implication: A plan-to-code preflight should compile each requirement into an executable acceptance object containing the invariant, positive cases, negative-space cases, required checks, evidence artifacts, threshold, owner, environment, and invalidation conditions.
implications.rationale: NIST supplies lifecycle context and measurement discipline, SWE-bench supplies execution-grounded task shape, Agent-SafetyBench supplies scenario breadth, and protected branches supply enforceable gate behavior.

implications.implication: Blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified must be distinct typed outcomes. Certification should require current evidence bound to the exact plan, implementation, dependencies, and evaluation context; an override should record scope, rationale, authority, compensating controls, and expiry without becoming a pass.
implications.rationale: The sources provide separate go or no-go, residual-risk, review, override, threshold, and invalidation controls; the four-state vocabulary is a proposed product-facing synthesis.

implications.implication: Use a two-layer gate: deterministic plan and repository preflight first, followed by adversarial scenario execution and independent or human review for risk-sensitive changes. Store negative results and untested surfaces as evidence, not only successful assertions.
implications.rationale: This combines NIST repeatable TEVV and independent review with threat-model and interaction-matrix evidence, while respecting GitHub's warning that agent review can miss problems.

implications.implication: Revalidation should trigger on material changes to plan text, source revision, merge base, dependency closure, builder or configuration, model or policy, evaluator version, or deployment context; certification should be revoked or downgraded until impacted checks complete.
implications.rationale: SLSA expectation comparison, GitHub stale-review behavior, and NIST continuous lifecycle management imply that evidence freshness is part of the claim.

implications.implication: A certification evidence bundle should include plan and source digests, dependency and builder provenance, acceptance and adversarial test outputs, scenario traces, metric definitions and uncertainty, review identities, overrides, residual risk, and the exact gate decision.
implications.rationale: These fields make the safety and completeness claim independently inspectable and allow later regression comparison.

novel_ideas.idea: Represent certification as a typed evidence graph rather than a boolean: a certificate node binds a plan digest, implementation digest, dependency closure, evaluator versions, scenario results, human decisions, residual risk, and expiry; each child evidence item can independently be valid, stale, missing, or contradicted.
novel_ideas.rationale: This extends provenance and lifecycle evidence into a product-readable certificate graph that prevents one stale child result from masquerading as a current global pass.

novel_ideas.idea: Generate a negative-space matrix mechanically from every acceptance criterion: intended use, omission, malformed input, adversarial instruction, permission boundary, tool failure, dependency drift, partial completion, rollback, and recovery. Require a disposition for each cell before certification.
novel_ideas.rationale: The idea turns threat-model and failure-mode coverage into a traceable completeness check instead of leaving negative space to reviewer intuition.

novel_ideas.idea: Use a revalidation trigger algebra: each evidence item declares the inputs it covers, and a change event invalidates only the affected subgraph while any high-risk invalidation immediately downgrades the aggregate certificate. The UI can show exactly why a certificate became uncertain or blocked.
novel_ideas.rationale: This combines SLSA expectation comparison and dependency scope with GitHub stale-approval semantics to make evidence freshness operational without rerunning unrelated checks.

novel_ideas.idea: Make overrides consumable as bounded control objects: require an approver, reason, affected acceptance objects, compensating tests, expiry, rollback action, and follow-up owner; display the result as overridden with residual risk, never as certified.
novel_ideas.rationale: The sources establish accountability, residual risk, leadership decision points, and explicit review gates; the bounded override object is a proposed implementation pattern.

unresolved_questions.question: No reviewed primary source specifies a universal canonical state machine or JSON schema named blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified for plan-to-code gates.
What minimum scenario count, repetition count, and statistical confidence are sufficient for a specific risk class, repository, or deployment context?
How should negative-space coverage be calibrated so that an agent cannot optimize for a visible scenario list while leaving unmodeled tool, permission, or recovery paths unsafe?
Which human roles may authorize an override for each risk tier, and what evidence threshold should automatically prohibit override rather than permit a documented exception?
